assessments.reasoning: Section 5(e) on printed p. 13 fixes the reference's lexical environment at func creation and retains the environment after scope exit. It distinguishes the default invocation-time value of that binding from a value declaration's creation-time value. On p. 14 the returned composition still uses the former call's f and g bindings, and the function array covers explicit capture of each iterator value. The title page identifies Levin, Version 3.0, and the September 18, 2021 rendering.

challenge.method: Compared caller-site lookup, snapshot-at-creation for all free variables, and loss of an enclosing call's bindings against section 5(a), (b), and (e)-(g). Checked the 2021 title-page date against the historical copyright page and the archive URL.
challenge.results: Levin's default is invocation-time access to a lexically selected binding. The value declaration provides the distinct snapshot case, and the composition example covers a returned func. The date labels this PDF rendering. The document carries older copyright years, and the filename's year does not establish the rendering date.

limitations: The review concerns nonlocal bindings of the current user-defined func in the dated Version 3.0 rendering. It provides no representation or copy-depth guarantee.
